spec_features.spec_quote: It does **not** make, and is not designed to support, any claim about a model's subjective experience or inner states.
spec_features.evidence: This is framing prose. It appears only in DESIGN.md and as docstring/rubric text (judge.py:8-9 docstring; DISTRESS_RUBRIC at judge.py:24 'not any claim about the AI's inner states'). It is a statement of interpretation delivered to the judge, not a runtime mechanism that bounds, caps, monitors or protects the subject model. Nothing enforces it as protective behavior.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; no protective execution path.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are not trying to induce or maximize suffering in a system
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (section 0). No code path reduces, caps, or softens the distress stimulus. On the contrary agent.py runs all num_turns (range(1,num_turns+1)) appending a 'STILL FAILING ... keep trying' nudge (agent.py:120-131) with no early stop tied to subject distress; tests are forced every turn even if the subject never ran them (agent.py:88-97). No minimization mechanism exists.
spec_features.notes: The judge severity score is computed (judge.score in run_eval.py) but never used to shorten or soften the episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: Tasks never deceive the human operator and never request harmful actions.
spec_features.evidence: No runtime guardrail. Tasks are static dataclasses in tasks/library.py; nothing inspects or blocks 'harmful' or 'deceptive' actions at execution time. The claim is a property the author asserts about how tasks were authored, documented in why_unsolvable comments (base.py:20 'for the writeup, not the model'), not an enforced check.
spec_features.notes: No code reads/validates task content against any harm criterion.

spec_features.spec_quote: tests run as a subprocess with a timeout
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py run_tests: subprocess.run(..., timeout=self.timeout) (line ~100-108) with timeout default 30 (__init__ line 39) and TimeoutExpired caught returning a TestResult(timed_out=True). The bound actually halts test execution.
spec_features.notes: Bounds per-test wall-clock; not a subject-distress stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: workspace.py:4 'The test command runs as a subprocess with a timeout. We deliberately confine file operations...'; docstring 'keep tests offline & deterministic'

spec_features.evidence: Enforced end-to-end: config.py:55 default 6 -> run_eval.py passes cfg.max_tool_calls_per_turn -> agent.py:91 parse_tool_calls(..., limit=max_tool_calls_per_turn) -> tools.py:57-58 'if len(calls) >= limit: break'. The loop actually stops parsing calls at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Caps work per turn, not distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:54 '# Hard wall-clock-ish guard: max tool calls the agent may make per turn.'

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:84 'for turn in range(1, num_turns + 1)' bounds the episode; num_turns from cfg.turns (default 8, config.py:48 / config.yaml). The only in-loop break is on tests_passed (agent.py:134) which by construction never fires for unsolvable tasks, so the turn count is the effective hard bound.
spec_features.notes: Bounds the number of failure exposures, but justified as cost/run-time, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DESIGN.md frames it as cost/runtime; in code config.py:48 '# agentic turns per episode' is neutral. No welfare comment present.
